entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},

content.text:
I sent you three pictures taken from the real running game just now: all 11 screens together, each approved picture next to the live game, and Screen 05 up close. The capture ran with no errors.

The game is also running live on port 5173, so if your app shows a preview pane you can open it and play it there.

How it looks against the approved pictures:

- **Closest: Screen 05.** The purple perforated walls, gold rings and winding cyan-and-pink water are all there. The rings still look flatter and more salmon than gold, the water is less glossy, and Benny sits a bit smaller.
- **Roughly right: Screen 07.** The ringed tube matches in shape, but the water runs straighter with heavy white foam banks.
- **Ending works: Screen 11.** The cartoon girl holds the towel and `FINAL SPIN COMPLETE` shows. She is the new cartoon girl on purpose, so she does not match the photo-style girl in the old picture.
- **Still clearly different: Screens 03, 04, 06, 08, 09 and 10.**
  - 03 is a very close, blurry view with no visible whirlpool funnel.
  - 04 shows no arrows on the water in this frame.
  - 06 has the camera facing the wall, so the arch does not read.
  - 08–10 have flat bright-magenta walls and straight striped water instead of the rich tunnel and S-curves.
- **Opening: Screens 01 and 02.** Both are real-time 3D with Benny and the girl, but framed much closer and simpler than the approved art.

Everything is saved: the resume check passed and the autosave matches GitHub. The pictures themselves are in the session's temporary folder, not in the repo.

old="  const rings05 = BIG05.b > 0 ? [sCam05 + BIG05.ringA] : ringSlots05.filter((s) => Math.abs(s - sF05) > 0.5);"
new="""  // round tunnel (default): the bay slots, with the slot ahead of ref ring B (depth 26) moved to RING_A05 (ref ring A)
  const rings05 = BIG05.b > 0 ? [sCam05 + BIG05.ringA]
    : ringSlots05.filter((s) => Math.abs(s - sF05) > 0.5).map((s) => (Math.abs(s - sCam05 - 26) < 3 ? sCam05 + RING_A05 : s));"""
assert old in t; t=t.replace(old,new)

new="""  // wave 9b: round tunnel again → the wave-8 lid pose (the wave-9 values above were fitted to the oval wall)
  const lid05 = K05 > 1.0005 || BIG05.b > 0
    ? { shape: 'slab' as const, angleDeg: 18, droopDeg: -38, size: 2.8, thickness: 0.45, stretch: 1.6, sink: 0.25 }
    : { shape: 'slab' as const, angleDeg: 8, droopDeg: -34, size: 2.2, thickness: 0.36, stretch: 1.0, sink: 0.1 };"""
assert old in t; t=t.replace(old,new)
old="""  const lids05 = rings05
    .map((s) => s + bandHalf05 + 0.15 + lid05.size * lid05.stretch * 1.04)
    .filter((s) => s > s05 + 4 && s < sF05 && !(s - sCam05 > 20 && s - sCam05 < 38));"""
new="""  const lids05 = K05 > 1.0005 || BIG05.b > 0
    ? rings05.map((s) => s + bandHalf05 + 0.15 + lid05.size * lid05.stretch * 1.04).filter((s) => s > s05 + 4 && s < sF05 && !(s - sCam05 > 20 && s - sCam05 < 38))
    : ringSlots05.map((s) => s - band05.width / 2 - lid05.size * 1.05).filter((s) => s > s05 + 4);"""
assert old in t; t=t.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(t)
EOF

Remember, I'm using my Google Flow videos for the beginning and ending of my game.

The beginning video shows the girl putting the clothes and hidden Benny into the washing machine.

The ending video shows the girl retrieving the towel and completes the story.

I do NOT need you to spend time recreating those video scenes as fully detailed playable 3D artwork.

Please focus your design specialists on the actual PLAYABLE GAMEPLAY, particularly Screens 03–09.

My biggest priority is still Screen 05, Flow Into the Current. I want the real playable environment to match my approved artwork as closely as possible, ideally 90–95% if achievable.

After Screen 05, concentrate on the other gameplay screens that look noticeably different from their approved references, especially 03, 04, 06, 07, 08 and 09.

Use the existing Marble World Labs assets, Blender and Three.js to improve the visuals.

IMPORTANT:

- Preserve my Google Flow opening and ending videos.
- Make the transition from the opening video into gameplay seamless.
- Make gameplay transition naturally into the ending video.
- Keep all gameplay mechanics and the 07→08 deep descent working.
- Don't waste credits rebuilding scenes that my videos already cover.
- Keep all ten specialist agents and the five-minute GitHub autosaves.

Please prioritize the playable 3D environments and show me separate full-size comparisons against my approved gameplay screens.

I want the playable game to look like the premium artwork I approved, not simply have the correct gameplay mechanics.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Screen 05: measure the projected gold rings (centre, radius, band thickness) in the approved image and in live
captures, by fitting circles to the gold pixels of each ring's upper arc.

    python3 -I tools/qa/ring_fit05.py OUT_DIR LABEL=image[:guessfile] ...

A circle (cx, cy, r) is scored by the share of gold pixels on its arc above its own centre line (HUD bar, title
banner and everything outside the frame are skipped). Each ring starts from a rough guess and is refined by an
exhaustive local search; the radius reported is the middle of the gold band, `thick` its radial thickness.
Writes OUT_DIR/rings.json, rings.md and one overlay PNG per image (fitted circles drawn on the picture) so the
fit can be checked by eye. Raw geometry only — not a fidelity score.
"""
import json, math, sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

W, H = 864, 1536
GUESS = {
    # rough starting circles (cx, cy, r, search half-ranges dx, dy, dr)
    'ref': {'A': (455, 535, 499, 45, 70, 60), 'B': (465, 455, 245, 30, 40, 30), 'C': (478, 453, 150, 20, 25, 20),
            'D': (490, 460, 96, 14, 18, 14), 'E': (495, 464, 62, 10, 12, 9), 'F': (497, 466, 42, 8, 9, 6)},
    'live': {'A': (512, 480, 370, 40, 50, 40), 'B': (505, 478, 232, 30, 35, 28), 'C': (500, 475, 160, 20, 22, 20),
             'D': (500, 472, 96, 14, 16, 14), 'E': (500, 471, 58, 10, 12, 9), 'F': (500, 470, 41, 8, 9, 6)},
}

def gold_mask(a):
    r, g, b = a[..., 0].astype(int), a[..., 1].astype(int), a[..., 2].astype(int)
    return (r > 160) & (r - b > 70) & (g > 45)

def arc_points(cx, cy, r, n=220):
    th = np.linspace(math.radians(8), math.radians(172), n)
    x = cx + r * np.cos(th); y = cy - r * np.sin(th)
    ok = (x >= 0) & (x < W) & (y >= 112) & (y < H) & ~((x > 112) & (x < 752) & (y > 114) & (y < 188))
    return x[ok].astype(int), y[ok].astype(int)

def score(m, cx, cy, r):
    x, y = arc_points(cx, cy, r)
    if len(x) < 30: return 0.0
    return float(m[y, x].mean())

def fit(m, g):
    cx0, cy0, r0, dx, dy, dr = g
    best = (-1, cx0, cy0, r0)
    for step in (4, 1):
        _, bx, by, br = best
        if step == 4: rx, ry, rr = range(-dx, dx + 1, 4), range(-dy, dy + 1, 4), range(-dr, dr + 1, 3)
        else: rx, ry, rr = range(-4, 5), range(-4, 5), range(-3, 4)
        for ox in rx:
            for oy in ry:
                for orr in rr:
                    cx, cy, r = bx + ox, by + oy, br + orr
                    s = (score(m, cx, cy, r - 2) + score(m, cx, cy, r) + score(m, cx, cy, r + 2)) / 3
                    if s > best[0]: best = (s, cx, cy, r)
    s, cx, cy, r = best
    # band edges along the radius (score falls below half of the peak)
    prof = {rr: score(m, cx, cy, rr) for rr in range(int(r) - 60, int(r) + 61)}
    pk = max(prof.values()); half = 0.5 * pk
    lo = r
    while lo - 1 in prof and prof[lo - 1] >= half: lo -= 1
    hi = r
    while hi + 1 in prof and prof[hi + 1] >= half: hi += 1
    return {'cx': cx, 'cy': cy, 'r': round((lo + hi) / 2, 1), 'thick': hi - lo + 1, 'gold_share': round(pk, 2)}

def main(argv):
    out = Path(argv[0]); out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    res = {}
    for spec in argv[1:]:
        label, path = spec.split('=', 1)
        im = Image.open(path).convert('RGB')
        if im.size != (W, H): im = im.resize((W, H), Image.LANCZOS)
        m = gold_mask(np.asarray(im))
        kind = 'ref' if 'references/' in path else 'live'
        guesses = dict(GUESS[kind])
        gfile = out / f'guess_{label}.json'
        if gfile.exists(): guesses.update({k: tuple(v) for k, v in json.loads(gfile.read_text()).items()})
        rings = {k: fit(m, g) for k, g in guesses.items()}
        res[label] = rings
        ov = im.copy(); d = ImageDraw.Draw(ov)
        for k, f in rings.items():
            cx, cy, r = f['cx'], f['cy'], f['r']
            for i in range(0, 360, 2):   # dashed circle
                if (i // 2) % 2: continue
                a0, a1 = math.radians(i), math.radians(i + 2)
                d.line([(cx + r * math.cos(a0), cy - r * math.sin(a0)), (cx + r * math.cos(a1), cy - r * math.sin(a1))], fill=(255, 255, 255), width=3)
                d.line([(cx + r * math.cos(a0), cy - r * math.sin(a0)), (cx + r * math.cos(a1), cy - r * math.sin(a1))], fill=(0, 0, 0), width=1)
            d.ellipse([cx - 4, cy - 4, cx + 4, cy + 4], outline=(255, 255, 255), fill=(0, 0, 0))
            d.text((cx + 6, cy - 6), k, fill=(255, 255, 0))
        ov.crop((0, 0, W, 900)).save(out / f'overlay_{label}.png')
    (out / 'rings.json').write_text(json.dumps(res, indent=1))
    lines = ['| image | ring | centre x | centre y | radius | band thick | radius ÷ next ring | gold share on arc |', '|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|']
    for label, rings in res.items():
        ks = list(rings)
        for i, k in enumerate(ks):
            f = rings[k]
            ratio = f"{f['r'] / rings[ks[i + 1]]['r']:.2f}" if i + 1 < len(ks) else '—'
            lines.append(f"| {label} | {k} | {f['cx']} | {f['cy']} | {f['r']} | {f['thick']} | {ratio} | {f['gold_share']} |")
    (out / 'rings.md').write_text('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
    print('\n'.join(lines))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv[1:])

== docs/FLOW_VIDEO.md:
# Google Flow opening / ending videos

The game can play the user's Google Flow videos as silent cinematics and hand over to the real-time 3D
game without a cut. Gameplay (03–10) is always real-time 3D; the videos only cover the cinematics.

## Where to put the files

| File | Plays | Hand-off |
|---|---|---|
| `public/video/intro.mp4` (or `.webm`) | at launch and on Replay, instead of the real-time 01 | the live 3D intro is held at the "girl walks away" moment (`T.cp01`) under the video, then revealed by a 0.7 s cross-fade a
| `public/video/ending.mp4` (or `.webm`) — optional | when Benny reaches 11, before the victory frame | the real-time 11 frame (the official cartoon girl holds the towel, Benny hidden, **FINAL SPIN COMPLETE**) is revea

If a file is missing, the real-time 3D cinematic plays instead. Videos are always muted and inline.
Tap skips the video (after 0.6 s).

## Recommended export

* Portrait 9:16 (1080×1920 or 720×1280) is best. Any ratio works edge to edge with no black bars and no stretching
  (`chooseVideoFit` in `src/ui/cinematicVideo.ts`):
  * **cover**: the clip is cropped to the phone when at least 78% of it stays visible. A 9:16 clip keeps 80% of its
    width on a 20:9 phone, so keep the girl, the towel and the washer door inside the centre ~80% of the frame.
    `?videoFocus=50% 40%` (CSS object-position) moves the crop centre for testing.
  * **fill**: if cropping would lose more (a 16:9 landscape Flow export, or a 9:16 clip on a 21:9 phone), the whole
    clip is shown over a soft blurred fill made from the same video frames instead of black bars.
* H.264 MP4 (AAC track optional — it is muted anyway). Keep it short (≈5–10 s) and under ~15 MB:
  the file is bundled into the Android APK.
* End the intro on the girl walking away from the closed washer door, seen from inside the drum if
  possible, so the cross-fade lands on the matching 3D shot. End the ending video just before the
  "girl holds the towel" pose.
* `.mp4` files are stored with Git LFS (see `.gitattributes`); the autosave backs them up automatically.

## Status (2026-11-15, account 3)

No Flow video is in the repository yet: `public/video/` holds only a placeholder note, so the game plays the
real-time 3D 01 opening. When the MP4 is ready, upload it and Claude will copy it to `public/video/intro.mp4`,
run `npm run test:cinematic`, rebuild the APK and push. No code change is needed.

## Testing

* Try a clip without copying it: `?introVideo=/path/under/project/root.mp4` (same for `endingVideo`);
  `?video=0` disables videos; QA captures (`?qa`) never play them.
* `npm run test:cinematic` — headless Chromium test of both paths (with a generated VP8 test clip and
  without any video). Result: `qa/cinematic_test.json`. Last run 2026-11-15: **pass** (overlay shown,
  3D held paused underneath, resumed after the fade and advanced 01 → 02; fallback without video OK).
  The test also checks edge-to-edge fit on a 20:9 phone (portrait clip → cover, landscape clip → blurred fill,
  no flat bar rows); screenshots in `qa/aspect/flow_video_*.png`.
  Note: this Chromium build has no H.264, so the automated test uses WebM; MP4 playback must be
  checked on a real Android device.

Implementation: `src/ui/cinematicVideo.ts`, hooks in `src/game/Game.ts` (`playIntroVideo`, `startOutro`).

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

content.text:
You were right, and the game is back on your BEFORE version. A fresh capture matches your BEFORE picture pixel for pixel, and Big Tunnel Test 1 is not in the working game.

## What went wrong
The bigger/oval tunnel was a misreading of your artwork, started in last night's unfinished work and continued by me. The top of your big front ring is hidden behind the title bar, so its sides were being paired with the next ring's top, which made round rings look like ovals. Measured one ring at a time, your approved rings are round.

## Ring measurements (radius in pixels)
| Ring | Approved | BEFORE | Test T1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (front ring that frames the picture) | 492 | 374 | 455 |
| B | 240 | 228 | 228 |
| C | 150 | 153 | 153 |
| D | 88 | 96 | 96 |

The vanishing point is in the same place in both pictures. BEFORE already has rings B, C and D within a few percent; the main structural gap is the front ring, which is 24% too small and floats inside the frame as an extra hoop.

## Test T1: one change only
- **What changed:** I moved only the front ring closer to the camera. Tunnel size, shape, camera, river and every other ring are identical to BEFORE.
- **Result:** the front ring now frames the left edge and passes behind the title bar, as in your artwork.
- **Still different:** the ring sits a little too high, so its arc is missing from the upper-right corner. Colours, gloss, lids and water are unchanged from BEFORE.
- **Status:** T1 is not switched on. The working game stays on BEFORE until you decide.

I sent the approved | BEFORE | T1 picture, the measurement overlay, and six separate full-size comparisons for screens 03, 04, 06, 07, 08 and 09.

## Your other instructions
- **Flow videos:** the game is already set up to play an opening and an ending video and hand over to gameplay, but no video file is in the project yet. Please upload the two videos here and I'll put them in and test the transitions.
- **Screens 01, 02 and 11:** no more 3D work on them.
- **Specialists:** all ten are kept and none is running, so nothing is spending credits in the background. After Screen 05 they go to 03, 04, 06, 07, 08 and 09, one screen at a time.
- **Last night's unfinished changes:** the water, foam and far coin-trail edits are also out of the working game, because BEFORE predates them. They are saved aside and can come back only as their own tests.
- **Safety:** the gameplay test passes 8 of 8 with the 07→08 drop intact. Everything is saved and GitHub matches, and I opened backup pull request #5, marked do-not-merge.

Do you want to keep T1? If yes, the next single test is lowering the near end of the tunnel so the front ring's arc shows in the upper-right corner.

 'google api key': r'AIza[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{35}',
 'jwt': r'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}\.eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}',
 'world labs key header with a value': r'WLT-Api-Key["\']?\s*[:=]\s*["\']?[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{16,}',
 'bearer token value': r'Authorization["\']?\s*[:=]\s*["\']?Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9_\-\.]{20,}',
 'generic api key assignment': r'(?i)(api[_-]?key|secret|password|access[_-]?token)["\']?\s*[:=]\s*["\'][A-Za-z0-9_\-\.]{24,}["\']',
 'email address (yahoo/gmail/outlook)': r'[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@(yahoo|gmail|outlook|hotmail|icloud)\.[a-z.]+',
}
hits = {k: [] for k in pats}; n = 0
for f in files:
    if not f or not os.path.isfile(f): continue
    if os.path.getsize(f) > 30_000_000: continue
    try: data = open(f,'rb').read()

    if b'\0' in data[:4096]: continue
    n += 1
    txt = data.decode('utf-8','ignore')
    for k, p in pats.items():
        for m in re.finditer(p, txt):
            s = m.group(0)
            hits[k].append((f, s[:12] + '…' if 'email' not in k else re.sub(r'^[^@]+', '***', s)))
print('text files scanned:', n)
for k, v in hits.items():
    print(f'{k}: {len(v)} hit(s)')
    seen = set()
    for f, s in v:
        if (f, s) in seen: continue
        seen.add((f, s))
        if len(seen) > 6: break
        print('    ', f[:90], '|', s)
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rainbow (josiahscalia5-dev/rainbow-): real Git LFS assets, Blender 5.3.0, Android SDK 34, World Labs plugin.
# Every step is non-fatal so a session always starts. Copy: scripts/cloud-env-setup.sh
if [ -d rainbow- ]; then
  # A pull that failed once leaves "access = basic" in .git/config and every later pull then asks for a
  # username (fails in a container). Clear it first; the session git proxy supplies the GitHub login.
  (cd rainbow- && git config --unset-all "lfs.https://github.com/josiahscalia5-dev/rainbow-.git/info/lfs.access"; true)
  (cd rainbow- && git lfs pull) || echo "rainbow: git lfs pull failed (the SessionStart hook retries)"
  (cd rainbow- && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund > /dev/null 2>&1) || echo "rainbow: npm ci failed"
  (cd rainbow- && bash scripts/setup-blender.sh) || echo "rainbow: blender setup failed"
  (cd rainbow- && bash scripts/setup-android-sdk.sh) || echo "rainbow: android sdk setup failed"
  (cd rainbow- && bash scripts/setup-worldlabs-plugin.sh) || echo "rainbow: worldlabs plugin setup failed"
fi
exit 0
